analysis: All 253 one-variable laws with <= 5 leaves per side, N <= 12, complete SAT - 213 have models of every size, 9 only N = 1, 24 violate divisor-closure (spectra missing exactly {2}, {3} or {2,3}), and the left combs x = (xx)x, x = ((xx)x)x, x = (((xx)x)x)x have spectra exactly Div(2), Div(3), Div(4); 0 UNKNOWN. H-C13-5 refuted.
assumptions: 253 laws (23 terms with <= 5 leaves; unordered pairs)
N = 1..12, complete SAT (conflict budget 2,000,000; UNKNOWN recorded)
cofiniteness is only suggested, not proved, by N <= 12
counterexamples: x = (xx)x has spectrum exactly {1, 2} (neither {1} nor cofinite)
x = x(x(xx)) has spectrum missing exactly 2 (N <= 12)
falsification: A law whose spectrum up to 12 is neither {1} nor of the form 'all N >= n0 plus a set of small N' (e.g. a law with models exactly at the even sizes).

hypothesis: H-C13-5 (bold): every one-variable law has anchored spectrum {1} or a cofinite set (all N beyond some bound), because such a law only constrains the orbit of each element under its own diagonal maps.
methodology: MagmaSAT with the anchor for every law and N; divisor-closure violations (N, d); spectra patterns; affine roots for comparison.
question: For every law t1(x) = t2(x) with t1 != t2 one-variable terms of at most 5 leaves, which N <= 12 admit an anchored model? Which spectra violate divisor-closure, and is every spectrum either {1} or cofinite?
